relevance.rationale: Part II of a programme constructing Weyl-group representations on the homology of the conormal variety via invariant eigendistributions and characteristic cycles, covering Springer theory (sec. 4), coherent families, harmonic polynomials, nilpotent orbital integrals, and an appendix proving the construction agrees with the Kazhdan-Lusztig one. The corpus's alg:delta-lambda-closure names its per-partition weight 'the signed Springer dimension' -- Delta_lambda = (-1)^{n(lambda)} dim V_lambda -- with no citation to the Springer literature anywhere in the tree ('Springer' appears in content/ only in that phrase and in publisher names). The same intersection carries the PROBE-4 prune, which turns on Kazhdan-Lusztig non-negativity being unable to supply a mixed-sign target. This paper is a geometric construction of exactly those two objects and of their comparison. Supporting, not core: the corpus's Delta_lambda value is already Lean-proved sorry-free, so nothing here aids a proof, and this is one construction of the Springer correspondence rather than the canonical primary for the degree/b-invariant statement the corpus's sign convention leans on.

keyResults.statement: Weyl-group representations are constructed on the (Borel-Moore) homology of the conormal variety via an integral formula for invariant eigendistributions, yielding the Springer representations.
keyResults.useForFolio: The geometric backdrop for the phrase 'signed Springer dimension' that alg:delta-lambda-closure uses without a source.

keyResults.statement: The homotopy action constructed here agrees with the Kazhdan-Lusztig construction of the Weyl-group action on the conormal variety.
keyResults.useForFolio: Relevant to the PROBE-4 prune's framing, which contrasts the mixed-sign Delta_lambda target against the non-negativity of Kazhdan-Lusztig multiplicities; the comparison shows the two constructions of the same W-action are not independent sources of a sign.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry, and no Springer-theory citation exists anywhere in the corpus despite the Delta_lambda value being described as a signed Springer dimension.

alg:delta-lambda-closure calls Delta_lambda 'the signed Springer dimension' with nothing behind the name. A citation should be added; a reviewer should also decide whether this construction or a more canonical Springer-correspondence source is the right primary for the sign convention.
